sections.html:
Wheat Ridge is a home rule city in Jefferson County that sits immediately west of Denver. Its municipal center is about 8.5 miles west-northwest of the Colorado State Capitol, at the junction of Interstate 70 and Colorado State Highway 391.

The city covers about 9.6 square miles at 5,348 feet of elevation and borders Arvada to the north, Lakeside, Mountain View and Denver to the east, Edgewater to the southeast, Lakewood to the south, and Applewood, Golden and Fairmount to the west and southwest. It sits on the western edge of the Great Plains, just east of the Front Range foothills.

Because it is small and completely surrounded by other places, a Wheat Ridge house is usually compared with ones in the adjoining suburbs as well as with others in the city.

sections.h2: How did Wheat Ridge become the Carnation City?
sections.html:
Wheat Ridge started as a rest stop for travelers during the Gold Rush of the late 1850s and became an agricultural community, known as the Carnation City, by the mid 1900s. Until the 1960s, orchards and crop fields defined the area, with homes and businesses scattered among them.

During the 1950s, the unincorporated parts of Jefferson County filled with housing for the Denver workforce, and commercial services grew along the main roads leading out of Denver. Utility and fire protection districts formed to serve those neighborhoods. Pressure from nearby cities to annex the land led residents to incorporate Wheat Ridge in 1969.

Today the city is largely built out. The Wheat Ridge Carnation Festival, held at Anderson Park in early August, remembers the carnation industry that followed World War II. The James H. Baugh House, an 1860 hand-hewn log cabin inside a farmhouse built around 1904, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and stands in the Wheat Ridge Historic Park.

sections.h2: What is the land like in Wheat Ridge, and what does it mean for a house?
sections.html:
Clear Creek runs east and then northeast through Wheat Ridge, and Lena Gulch, a tributary, flows northeast through the southwest part of the city. Several small lakes and reservoirs sit along those waterways.

  • Crown Hill Lake, Kestrel Pond and North Henry Lee Reservoir are in the south-central part of the city.
  • West Lake, Tabor Lake and Prospect Lake lie along Clear Creek in the west-central part.
  • The Köppen classification for the city is humid continental.

Living near a creek or a lake is a plus for many buyers, but they will ask about drainage and flood zones. If your property is near Clear Creek or Lena Gulch, gather any drainage or flood paperwork you have before you list.

sections.h2: What housing and age mix does Wheat Ridge have?
sections.html:
Wheat Ridge is one of the older, more settled suburbs in the Denver area. The 2020 Census counted 14,663 households, and about 35.5 percent were one-person households. Another 15.5 percent had someone age 65 or older living alone.

The median age is 41.1, and 20.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. Heirs and downsizing owners are common sellers in a community with that age profile, and they often want the house sold without prep work. The 2020 Census also found 15,471 housing units, of which 5.2 percent were vacant.

sections.h2: What are Wheat Ridge's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Wheat Ridge requires a license for short-term rentals and caps the number of whole-home licenses in each of its four council districts. The ordinance took effect May 1, 2021, and the city also collects a 10 percent lodgers' tax on completed reservations, due on the 20th of each month.

The cap equals 2 percent of single-family and two-unit dwellings in each district. As of the city's February 2026 table:

Council districtMaximum whole-home licensesRemainingWaitlisted
District I49035
District II52015
District III5490
District IV3701

Three rules affect anyone buying or selling a house with a short-term rental in mind. Only the legal owner can apply, and a new purchase requires a copy of the deed. The licenses are non-transferable, so a buyer cannot simply take over yours. And owner-occupied partial-home rentals are not subject to the cap.

The cap matters most when a buyer plans a whole-home rental: if your buyer wants to run the house as a whole-home rental in a district with no remaining licenses, they join a waitlist. Read the rules on the City of Wheat Ridge Short Term Rentals page and contact license@wheatridge.gov with questions.

sections.h2: Does Wheat Ridge allow gardens, bees and chickens on a residential lot?
sections.html:
Yes. City Council adopted Ordinance 1491 in May 2011, which supports urban agriculture. Homeowners can grow and sell produce and keep animals such as bees and chickens, under the city's rules.

  • Urban gardens, including community gardens, are allowed in every zone district.
  • Farmers' markets are allowed in any zone district except residential areas where the main use is a single or two-family home, and they need a business license.
  • Produce stands need a business license, and on residential property they must also follow the home occupation rules.

If you have a garden bed, a coop or a hive on your lot, tell your buyer what is there and what you have followed from the city's rules.

sections.h2: When are Jefferson County property taxes due for a Wheat Ridge house?
sections.html:
Jefferson County sends one tax notice by the end of January, and it includes coupons for each due date. Taxes are collected in arrears, so each bill covers the prior year.

Payment2026 date
First installmentMonday, March 2, 2026 (the county was closed on Saturday, February 28)
Full paymentThursday, April 30, 2026
Second installmentMonday, June 15, 2026

Delinquent notices go out in July. Unpaid real property taxes are advertised in a local newspaper for three consecutive weeks starting in early October, and the annual tax lien sale is held online in November. The Treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden, open Monday to Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. and closed Fridays. The call number is 303-271-8330.

The full schedule is on the Jefferson County Treasurer's Important Dates page.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale look like for a Wheat Ridge homeowner?
sections.html:
A cash buyer does not need a mortgage, so the sale does not depend on a lender's appraisal or approval. You review an offer, accept it or not, and pick a closing date with the title company.

  • You can sell the house as-is, without a repair list.
  • You choose a closing date that suits your move.
  • If the house is a rental, check that the lease and rental license questions are settled first.
  • The title company records the deed with Jefferson County.

Some owners prefer to avoid showings and open houses, which a cash sale skips.

faqs.q: How many people live in Wheat Ridge, Colorado?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 32,398 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate shown at the top of this page is 32,081.

faqs.q: When are Jefferson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half payments are due in late February (the first installment for 2025 taxes fell on March 2, 2026), full payment is due April 30, and the second half is due June 15. Jefferson County sends one notice in January.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Wheat Ridge?
faqs.a: Only with a license. Whole-home licenses are capped by council district, and as of February 2026 only District III had licenses remaining. Licenses are non-transferable, and only the legal owner can apply.

faqs.q: Does Wheat Ridge allow backyard chickens and bees?
faqs.a: The city's urban agriculture ordinance, adopted in 2011, lets homeowners keep animals such as bees and chickens, within the city's regulations. Check the current rules before you list or buy.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wheat Ridge house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, kitchen or flooring first.
